title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
hook: How does a Transformer decide which words to focus on? It compares queries to keys, turns similarities into weights, and mixes values. Edit the matrices below to see it happen.

symbols.meaning: Normalizes scores to a probability distribution

equation.caption: Scaled dot-product attention. When scaling is off, we omit the division by sqrt(d_k).

steps: Check: each row of weights sums to 1. Row sums: {{rowSums}}

explorations.title: Equal scores
explorations.predict: If all scores are equal, what will the attention weights be?
explorations.observe: All weights become 0.5, so the output is the average of the value vectors.
explorations.why: When scores are equal, softmax gives uniform weights: each weight = 1/n. The output is then the average of the value vectors.

explorations.title: Dominant score
explorations.predict: If one score is much larger than the other, what happens to the weights?
explorations.observe: The weight for the first key becomes close to 1, so the output is almost exactly the first value vector.
explorations.why: A large score gap makes softmax assign nearly all weight to the largest score. The output then approximates that value vector.

self_tests.name: Output equals weighted sum of V
self_tests.expect: approx(out.output[0][0], out.weights[0][0]*inp.V[0][0] + out.weights[0][1]*inp.V[1][0], 1e-6) && approx(out.output[0][1], out.weights[0][0]*inp.V[0][1] + out.weights[0][1]*inp.V[1][1], 1e-6)

limitation: This demo uses tiny 2x2 matrices and does not include multiple attention heads, masking, or training. It only illustrates the core computation of scaled dot-product attention.
misconception: Attention weights are not learned parameters; they are computed from the inputs Q and K. The only learned parameters in a Transformer are the projection matrices that produce Q, K, and V.

claims.text: Scaled dot-product attention computes softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V.
The scaling factor 1/sqrt(d_k) prevents the dot products from growing too large, which would make the softmax very peaked.
In this toy setup, we use 2x2 matrices and omit multi-head attention and masking.

outcomes.outcome: Compute similarity scores between queries and keys
Apply softmax to obtain attention weights
Compute the output as a weighted sum of values
Explain the effect of scaling by 1/sqrt(d_k)
Verify that each row of weights sums to 1
Verify that the output equals the weighted sum of V
